title: Python turtle reference
summary: Commands you can click to insert, with what each one does.

items.label: forward
items.hint: Move the turtle forward. The number is how many steps.

items.label: backward
items.hint: Move the turtle backward without turning.

items.label: right
items.hint: Turn clockwise by this many degrees.

items.label: left
items.hint: Turn anticlockwise by this many degrees.

items.label: goto
items.hint: Jump to a position. (0, 0) is the centre; x goes right, y goes up.
items.shows: From the centre to (80, 60)

items.label: setheading
items.hint: Face a direction. 0 is right, 90 is up, 180 is left.
items.shows: setheading(90): facing up

items.label: home
items.hint: Go back to the centre, facing right.
items.shows: Back to the centre, facing right

items.label: penup
items.hint: Lift the pen so moving does not draw.
items.shows: Pen up for the middle part

items.label: pendown
items.hint: Put the pen down so moving draws again.
items.shows: Pen down again for the last part

items.label: pensize
items.hint: Set how thick the line is.
items.shows: pensize(1), then pensize(8)

items.label: pencolor
items.hint: Set the line colour, using a colour name.

items.label: dot
items.hint: Draw a filled dot of this size.

items.label: write
items.hint: Write text at the turtle's position.

items.label: fillcolor
items.hint: Choose the colour to fill shapes with.

items.label: begin_fill / end_fill
items.hint: Everything drawn between these two lines is filled in.
items.example:
fillcolor("orange")
begin_fill()
for i in range(4):
    forward(60)
    right(90)
end_fill()

items.label: bgcolor
items.hint: Set the background colour.

items.label: hideturtle
items.hint: Hide the turtle so only the drawing shows.
items.shows: The line stays; the turtle is hidden

items.label: speed
items.hint: How fast the turtle moves, from 1 (slow) to 10 (fast).

items.label: clear
items.hint: Wipe the drawing.

items.label: circle
items.hint: Draw a circle with this radius.
items.shows: circle(50) starts at the turtle and curves left

items.label: square (loop)
items.hint: Draw a square by repeating forward and right four times.

items.label: for loop
items.hint: Repeat the indented lines this many times.
items.example:
for i in range(5):
    forward(15)
    penup()
    forward(10)
    pendown()
items.shows: range(5): five dashes

items.label: while loop
items.hint: Repeat the indented lines for as long as the condition is true.
items.example:
r = 10
while r < 60:
    circle(r)
    r = r + 15
items.shows: A circle each time, while r < 60

items.label: ask and reply
items.hint: Ask a question, store the typed answer, and use it in a reply.
items.example:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Hello, " + name)
items.shows: Asks for a name, then says hello

items.label: check then convert
items.hint: Check typed text with isdigit before turning it into a number.
items.shows: A checked ticket total

items.label: running total
items.hint: Start the total at 0 once, then add to it on every pass.
items.example:
total = 0
while total < 10:
    total += int(input("Add: "))
    print("Total: " + str(total))
print("Done")
items.shows: Adds typed numbers until the total reaches 10

items.label: menu loop
items.hint: A menu that keeps showing until a break runs.
items.shows: A till that adds $5 until you pay

items.label: if / else
items.hint: Do one thing or the other, depending on a condition.
items.shows: Red when x > 0, else blue

items.label: every other
items.hint: i % 2 == 0 is true on every second pass.
items.shows: Red and blue sides, taking turns

items.label: variable
items.hint: Give a value a name, so you can reuse and change it.
items.shows: length = 120, then half of it

items.label: named turn
items.code:
sides = ‹5›
for i in range(sides):
    forward(‹60›)
    right(360 / sides)
items.hint: Name the number of sides once; the turn is worked out from it.
items.example:
sides = 6
for i in range(sides):
    forward(60)
    right(360 / sides)
items.shows: A hexagon: change sides and the turn follows

items.label: counter step
items.hint: Use the counter i to make each pass different.
items.shows: A square spiral: each line longer than the last

items.label: grow value
items.code:
‹size› = ‹5›
for i in range(‹20›):
    forward(‹size›)
    right(‹90›)
    ‹size› = ‹size› + ‹5›
items.hint: Change a value every pass: read the old one, store a new one.
items.example:
size = 5
for i in range(30):
    forward(size)
    right(90)
    size = size + 5
items.shows: The same spiral, grown by an update

items.label: list
items.hint: Keep many values in order under one name. The first item is place 0.

items.label: for each item
items.hint: Work through a list, one item at a time.
items.example:
pensize(6)
for c in ["red", "blue", "green"]:
    pencolor(c)
    forward(40)
items.shows: One line per colour in the list

items.label: def (function)
items.hint: Name a group of steps, then run it by calling its name.
items.example:
def zigzag():
    left(45)
    forward(30)
    right(90)
    forward(30)
    left(45)

zigzag()
zigzag()
zigzag()
items.shows: Defined once, called three times

items.label: print
items.hint: Show text or a value in the output box.

items.label: random number
items.hint: Pick a random whole number between two values.

items.label: onscreenclick
items.code:
def ‹stamp›(x, y):
    goto(x, y)
    dot(‹20›)

onscreenclick(‹stamp›)
listen()
mainloop()
items.hint: Run a function every time the picture is clicked. It receives the click position.
items.example:
def stamp(x, y):
    goto(x, y)
    dot(20)

penup()
stamp(-60, 30)
stamp(50, -20)
hideturtle()
items.shows: After two clicks

items.label: onkey
items.hint: Run a function every time a key is pressed. Click the picture first so it receives keys.
items.example:
def go_up():
    forward(20)

go_up()
go_up()
go_up()
items.shows: After pressing Up three times

items.label: ontimer
items.hint: Run a function again after a number of milliseconds. A function can start its own timer.

items.label: numinput
items.hint: Ask for a number in a pop-up. The answer is None if the pop-up is cancelled.

items.label: textinput
items.hint: Ask for text in a pop-up.

items.label: input
items.hint: Show a question in the console, wait for an answer, and store what was typed. It is always text.

items.label: join text
items.hint: Join pieces of text into one with +. Spaces only appear where they are inside the quotes.

items.label: str
items.hint: Turn a number into text, so it can be joined: "Score: " + str(score).

items.label: int
items.hint: Turn text made of digits, such as "12", into a whole number you can calculate with.

items.label: isdigit
items.hint: True if the text is all digits (0 to 9) and not empty, so int() will work on it.

items.label: add to (+=)
items.hint: Add to a variable: total += 5 is short for total = total + 5.

items.label: break
items.hint: Leave the loop straight away; the program carries on after it.

items.label: new turtle
items.hint: Make another turtle with its own name. Put the name and a dot in front of a command to give it to that turtle.

items.label: dictionary
items.hint: Values stored under names (keys). One dictionary can hold everything about one thing.

items.label: dictionary value
items.hint: The value stored under that key. The key goes in quotes. Assign to it to change it: star["speed"] = 8.

items.label: class
items.hint: A new kind of object. __init__ runs when one is made; self.name = value stores a value in that object.

items.label: method
items.hint: A function inside a class. Call it on one object: star.move(). self is that object.

items.label: strip and lower
items.hint: strip() removes spaces at the ends; lower() and upper() change the capitals. Each gives back new text.

items.label: split
items.hint: Cut text into a list of words at the spaces: "go north".split() is ["go", "north"].

items.label: in
items.hint: True if the item is in the list (or the key is in the dictionary, or the letters are in the text).

items.label: join
items.hint: Join a list of texts into one, with the text in quotes between each: "lamp, key".

items.label: remove from a list
items.hint: Take an item out of a list. It stops with a ValueError if the item is not there, so check with in first.

items.label: sort
items.hint: Put a list in order (A to Z, or smallest first). It changes the list itself.

items.label: try and except
items.hint: Run lines that might fail. If the named error happens, the except lines run instead of the program stopping.

items.label: write a file
items.hint: "w" makes the file, or empties it first if it is already there, then writes. with closes the file at the end.

items.label: read a file
items.hint: Opens the file to read and gives you all of it as one piece of text.

items.label: save with json
items.code:
import json

with open("‹game.json›", "w") as f:
    json.dump(‹game›, f)
items.hint: Writes a dictionary or list to a file as JSON text.

items.label: load with json
items.code:
import json

with open("‹game.json›") as f:
    ‹game› = json.load(f)
items.hint: Reads JSON text back into the dictionary or list that was saved.

items.label: a missing file
items.hint: The first time, there is no file: catch FileNotFoundError instead of stopping.

items.label: read a CSV
items.code:
import csv

with open("‹music.csv›") as f:
    ‹rows› = list(csv.DictReader(f))
items.hint: Each row of the file becomes a dictionary, keyed by the column names in the first line. Every value is text.

items.label: count with a dictionary
items.hint: One count for each different value: add 1 if the key is there already, or start it at 1.

items.label: a text bar
items.hint: "#" * 5 is #####. ljust pads the label to the same width, so the bars line up.

items.label: test with assert
items.hint: A test case: nothing happens if it is true; the program stops with AssertionError if it is not.

items.label: read a CSV with pandas
items.hint: Reads the whole file into a table (a DataFrame). Numbers stay numbers.

items.label: filter a table
items.hint: Keeps the rows where the test is true, as a smaller table.

items.label: an app with Gradio
items.code:
import gradio as gr

def ‹answer›(‹choice›):
    return ‹"You chose " + choice›

gr.Interface(fn=‹answer›, inputs=gr.Dropdown(‹["pop", "rock"]›), outputs="text").launch()
items.hint: Gradio calls your function with what was chosen, and shows what it returns.

items.label: a quiz question
items.hint: A question as a dictionary, and a Radio input made from it: the student picks one of the choices, and the function gets that text.

items.label: ask an API
items.hint: Asks an API at that address (params become the ?query string) and turns the JSON reply into dictionaries and lists. Plan for no connection.

items.label: a Flask route
items.hint: Joins an address to a function. What the function returns is the page.

items.label: a page from a template
items.hint: A template is HTML with gaps: {{ }} shows a value, {% for %} repeats a part for each item.

items.label: an address with a part that changes
items.hint: <name> matches any word in that place of the address, and is passed to the function.

items.label: read a form
items.hint: A form with method='post' sends each box that has a name='...' attribute. request.form looks them up by that name.

items.label: go to another page
items.hint: Sends the browser on to another address, such as back home after a form.

items.label: add a row to a CSV
items.code:
with open("‹members.csv›", "a", newline="") as f:
    csv.writer(f).writerow([‹name›, ‹group›])
items.hint: "a" adds to the end of the file instead of emptying it. Each list becomes one row.

items.label: send JSON
items.hint: Return a dictionary and Flask sends it as JSON, for other programs to read.

items.label: a FastAPI route
items.hint: The type after each parameter (int, str, float) is checked: a wrong value gets an error reply (422) before your code runs.

items.label: test a model
items.hint: Shuffle, then keep some examples back. Train on one part; test only on the other.

items.label: train and score a model
items.code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

‹X_train›, ‹X_test›, ‹y_train›, ‹y_test› = train_test_split(‹X›, ‹y›, test_size=‹0.25›, random_state=‹1›)
‹model› = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=‹1›)
‹model›.fit(‹X_train›, ‹y_train›)
print(‹model›.score(‹X_test›, ‹y_test›))
items.hint: fit learns from the training examples; score tests on the held-back ones (1.0 is 100%).

items.label: predict with a model
items.hint: The new example needs the same columns, in the same order, as the training data.
